requirement_text.REQ-365: Per explicit user decision: platform-level help (shared screens like login-routing that no tenant owns) is authored through the BA-agent/REQ-ANALYST pipeline, matching the exact platform-vs-tenant split already established for UAT scenarios (REQ-358's scope field, REQ-359's BA-persona/REQ-ANALYST split, REQ-360's login-routing scenario as the worked platform example). This requirement is the authoring-path equivalent for help content: it does not re-derive that split, it applies it. . SCOPE: wherever REQ-363's design placed platform-scope help content (a dedicated table/schema, per that requirement's own acceptance criterion), this requirement adds the write path/tooling REQ-ANALYST (or, once REQ-359 lands, whichever role it specifies for platform content) actually uses to author it — this could be as simple as a direct context-module call analogous to REQ-364's tenant-scoped one, scoped to the platform table instead, reusing REQ-364's create/update/publish/reconfirm shape rather than inventing a parallel one. Explicitly NOT a new UI — platform help authoring is agent-pipeline-driven, matching how platform-scope UAT scenarios are authored (a file/record written by an agent, not a form filled by a human). . FIRST REAL CONTENT: author help for the login-routing screen (the same screen REQ-360's UAT scenario covers) as this requirement's own worked, real example — proves the authoring path end-to-end rather than shipping an authoring mechanism with zero real content using it.

FAIL immediately on any applicable invariant failing -- all BLOCKER, no partial credit.
